about: House recipes, batch 04 (slice C): written by Claude in a Max-plan session, original, ai-draft. Nutrition is a per-serve estimate kept as data only.

recipes.title: Czech Kulajda Dill and Potato Soup
recipes.summary: Creamy South Bohemian soup of potato, dill and a gently poached egg, sharpened with vinegar.
steps: Melt the butter in a large pot and soften the onion and mushrooms for 6 minutes, until the mushroom liquid has cooked off.
Stir in the flour for 1 minute, then add the stock and potato and simmer for 15 minutes, until the potato is completely tender.
Stir in the cream and most of the dill and simmer gently for 3 minutes, then season with salt and white pepper.
Bring a wide pan of water with the vinegar to a bare simmer and poach the eggs for 3 minutes, until the whites are set.
Ladle the soup into bowls, top each with a poached egg and the remaining dill.
notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until the whites are fully set, and cook the yolks through for anyone pregnant, elderly or unwell.

recipes.title: Polish Zurek Sour Rye Soup
recipes.summary: Tangy soup of soured rye flour, potato and smoked sausage, served with halved boiled eggs.
steps: Mix the rye flour with the warm water, garlic and bay leaf in a jar and leave covered at room temperature for 3 days, until sour and bubbly.
Brown the sausage in a large pot for 4 minutes, until it releases its fat, then add the carrot, potato and stock.
Simmer for 15 minutes, until the potato is tender, then strain in the soured rye starter and stir.
Simmer for 8 minutes, stirring, until the soup thickens slightly, then add the marjoram, horseradish, salt and pepper.
Boil the eggs for 9 minutes until firm, peel and halve them, and serve them in the bowls of soup.
notes: Food safety: heat the sausage until steaming hot and above 75°C in the centre, and boil the eggs until the yolks are firm.
The soured starter is made with cooked-through simmering, so always boil the soup for 8 minutes before serving.

recipes.title: Hungarian Halaszle Fisherman's Soup
recipes.summary: Fiery paprika-red river fish soup in the style of the Danube, built on onion and tomato.

items: 600g firm white fish fillets, cut in chunks

steps: Soften the onions in the oil for 10 minutes, until deep golden and sweet, then stir in both paprikas off the heat.
Add the tomatoes, capsicum and stock and simmer for 15 minutes, until the vegetables are soft and the broth is dark red.
Slide in the fish chunks and simmer gently for 5 minutes, until the fish is opaque and flakes easily.
Season with salt, scatter with parsley and serve with lemon slices.
notes: Food safety: cook the fish until opaque and flaking, and keep chilled until it goes into the pot.
Do not stir hard once the fish is added or it will break up.

recipes.title: Polish Mizeria Cucumber Salad
recipes.summary: Thin cucumber slices in a cool sour cream and dill dressing, a summer staple beside grilled meat.
steps: Toss the cucumber with a good pinch of salt and let it sit in a colander for 10 minutes, then squeeze out the liquid.
Stir the sour cream with the vinegar, sugar, dill and spring onion until smooth.
Fold the cucumber through the dressing, season with pepper and serve very cold.
notes: Serve within an hour of dressing or the cucumber will release more water and thin the sauce.

recipes.title: Romanian Ciorba de Perisoare Meatball Sour Soup
recipes.summary: Sour vegetable soup studded with herby pork and rice meatballs, finished with sour cream.
steps: Mix the pork, rice, egg, half the parsley, salt and pepper and roll into 24 small meatballs.
Simmer the onion, carrots, celery and capsicum in the stock for 12 minutes, until almost tender, then stir in the tomato paste.
Drop in the meatballs and simmer for 15 minutes, until the rice in them is tender and the centres reach 75°C.
Stir in the lemon juice, then temper the sour cream with a ladle of hot broth and stir it back in.
Serve in deep bowls scattered with the remaining parsley.
notes: Food safety: cook the meatballs until they reach 75°C in the centre and no pink remains.
Do not boil once the sour cream is added or it may split.

recipes.title: Serbian Ajvar Roasted Pepper Relish
recipes.summary: Smoky roasted pepper and aubergine spread that keeps for weeks in the fridge.
steps: Roast the capsicums and aubergine on a tray at 220°C for 45 minutes, turning once, until the skins are blistered and the flesh collapsed.
Rest them covered for 15 minutes, then peel off the skins and discard the seeds and stalks.
Chop the flesh finely and cook it in a wide pan with the garlic and half the oil for 15 minutes, stirring, until thick and jammy.
Stir in the vinegar, salt and sugar and the remaining oil, and cook 2 minutes more.
Cool and spoon into a clean jar, then chill.
notes: Store in a clean jar with a film of oil in the fridge for up to 2 weeks.

recipes.title: Czech Bramborak Garlic Potato Pancakes
recipes.summary: Crisp grated potato pancakes with marjoram and plenty of garlic.
steps: Squeeze the grated potato in a clean tea towel to remove the liquid, then mix with the garlic, egg, flour, marjoram and salt.
Heat the oil in a large frying pan over medium heat and spoon in flat pancakes the size of a saucer.
Cook for 4 minutes each side, until deep golden and crisp at the edges.
Drain on paper and serve hot.
notes: Food safety: cook the egg-bound batter until the pancakes are golden and set all the way through.

recipes.title: Russian Syrniki Quark Pancakes
recipes.summary: Small golden fried cheese pancakes, soft inside, served with sour cream.
steps: Mash the ricotta with the egg, sugar, vanilla and salt, then fold in the flour to a soft, tacky dough.
Shape into 12 small thick discs with floured hands.
Fry in the oil over medium-low heat for 3 minutes each side, until deep golden and just firm.
Serve warm with a spoonful of sour cream.
notes: Food safety: cook until the centres are hot and set, as the mixture contains raw egg.

recipes.title: Russian Okroshka Cold Buttermilk Soup
recipes.summary: Chilled summer soup of buttermilk, cucumber, radish, egg and dill.
steps: Boil the eggs for 9 minutes until the yolks are firm, cool in cold water, peel and chop.
Combine the cucumber, radish, potato, ham, eggs, dill and spring onions in a large bowl.
Whisk the buttermilk with the cold water and a pinch of salt and pour over, then chill for 30 minutes before serving.
notes: Food safety: boil the eggs until the yolks are firm, and keep the soup refrigerated, eating within a day.

recipes.title: Russian Olivier Salad
recipes.summary: Diced potato, egg, pickles and peas bound with a tangy dressing, the classic party salad.
steps: Boil the potato and carrots in salted water for 18 minutes, until a knife slides in easily, then cool and dice.
Boil the eggs for 9 minutes until firm, then cool, peel and dice them.
Blanch the peas in boiling water for 2 minutes, drain and cool.
Fold everything together with the mayonnaise and sour cream, season and chill for 30 minutes before serving.
notes: Food safety: use fully cooked chicken, heated to 75°C before cooling, and keep the salad chilled, eating within 2 days.

recipes.title: Georgian Pkhali Spinach Walnut Balls
recipes.summary: Cold spinach and walnut paste with garlic and herbs, shaped into little balls and topped with pomegranate.
steps: Blanch the spinach in boiling water for 2 minutes until wilted and bright green, then cool, squeeze dry and chop very finely.
Blend the walnuts, garlic, coriander leaves, vinegar and ground coriander to a coarse paste.
Mix the paste with the spinach, onion and salt until it holds together when squeezed.
Roll into 18 balls, top with pomegranate seeds and chill until firm, about 30 minutes.
notes: Chill in a covered container for up to 2 days.

recipes.title: Czech Cesnecka Garlic Soup
recipes.summary: Clear garlic and caraway soup with crisp bread croutons and a poached egg.
steps: Toss the bread in the olive oil and bake at 200°C for 10 minutes, until crisp and golden.
Soften the garlic in the butter for 2 minutes without browning, then add the stock, caraway, marjoram and potato.
Simmer for 15 minutes, until the potato is tender, then season.
Poach the eggs in barely simmering water with the vinegar for 3 minutes, until the whites are set.
Ladle into bowls and top with croutons and an egg.
notes: Food safety: poach the eggs until the whites are set, and cook fully for anyone vulnerable.

recipes.title: Polish Zupa Ogorkowa Pickle Soup
recipes.summary: Comforting potato soup soured with grated dill pickles and their brine.
steps: Soften the onion in the butter for 6 minutes, then add the carrots, parsnip, potato and stock.
Simmer for 18 minutes until all the vegetables are tender.
Add the grated pickles and brine and simmer for 5 minutes more.
Temper the sour cream with a ladle of hot soup, stir it in off the heat, then add the dill and season.
notes: Do not boil after adding the sour cream.

recipes.title: Russian Shchi Cabbage Soup
recipes.summary: Long-simmered beef and cabbage soup with a sour finish and dill.

items: 400g beef chuck, cut in small cubes

steps: Simmer the beef with the water, stock and bay leaves for 35 minutes, skimming, until the meat is tender.
Add the onion, carrot and potato and simmer for 10 minutes, until nearly soft.
Add the cabbage and tomato paste and cook 10 minutes more, until the cabbage has softened.
Season with the vinegar, salt and pepper and serve with dill and a spoonful of sour cream.
notes: Food safety: simmer the beef until tender and steaming hot throughout, at least 75°C in the centre of the pieces.

recipes.title: Lithuanian Saltibarsciai Cold Beet Soup
recipes.summary: Vivid pink chilled beetroot soup with buttermilk, cucumber and boiled egg.
steps: Boil the beetroot in water for 30 minutes until a knife slides in easily, then cool and coarsely grate.
Boil the eggs for 9 minutes until firm, cool, peel and halve.
Whisk the buttermilk with the water and mix with the beetroot, cucumber, spring onion and dill, then season with salt and chill for 1 hour.
Serve cold with the eggs and the hot potato alongside.
notes: Food safety: boil the eggs until the yolks are firm, and keep the soup refrigerated, eating within a day.

recipes.title: Austrian Frittatensuppe Pancake Soup
recipes.summary: Clear beef broth with ribbons of thin herb pancake and chives.
steps: Whisk the flour, milk, eggs, a pinch of salt and nutmeg into a smooth thin batter.
Melt a little butter in a non-stick pan and cook thin pancakes for 2 minutes each side, until set and lightly golden.
Roll the pancakes up, slice them into thin ribbons and add the chives.
Heat the stock until steaming and ladle over the ribbons to serve.
notes: Food safety: cook the pancakes until fully set and golden, as they contain raw egg.

recipes.title: German Warmer Kartoffelsalat Bacon Potato Salad
recipes.summary: Warm waxy potatoes in a tangy bacon and onion dressing, the south German way.
steps: Boil the potatoes whole for 20 minutes, until a knife slides in easily, then peel while warm and slice.
Fry the bacon until crisp for 6 minutes, then add the onion and cook 4 minutes, until soft.
Add the stock, vinegar, mustard and sugar and simmer 2 minutes, then pour over the warm potato with the oil.
Toss gently, season and scatter with chives.
notes: Food safety: cook the bacon until crisp and hot throughout, and refrigerate leftovers promptly.

recipes.title: Slovenian Jota Bean and Sauerkraut Soup
recipes.summary: Hearty soup of beans, sauerkraut and potato with smoked meat from the Karst region.
steps: Cook the bacon and onion in the oil for 8 minutes, until the fat renders and the onion softens, then add the garlic and paprika.
Add the potato, sauerkraut, water and bay leaf and simmer for 25 minutes, until the potato is soft.
Stir the flour into a ladle of the soup, then add it back with the beans and simmer 8 minutes, until slightly thickened.
Season to taste with salt and pepper and serve hot with bread.
notes: Food safety: cook the bacon until crisp at the edges and steaming hot.

recipes.title: Swedish Raggmunk Potato Pancakes
recipes.summary: Thin crisp potato pancakes served with crisp bacon and a spoonful of lingonberry-style preserve.
steps: Whisk the milk, eggs, flour and salt to a batter and stir in the grated potato.
Fry the bacon in a wide pan for 5 minutes until crisp, and keep warm.
Heat the butter in the pan and spoon in thin pancakes, then cook 3 minutes each side, until golden and crisp.
Serve with the bacon and cranberry sauce.
notes: Food safety: cook the bacon until crisp and the pancakes until set throughout.

recipes.title: Swedish Ärtsoppa Yellow Pea Soup
recipes.summary: Thick yellow split pea soup with ham and mustard, a Thursday tradition.

items: 300g ham hock, or diced cooked ham

steps: Put the peas, water, onion, carrot and ham in a large pot and bring to a boil, skimming until the foam stops rising.
Simmer gently for 60 minutes, until the peas are completely soft and the soup thick.
Take out the ham, shred the meat and return it, then add the herbs, salt and pepper.
Serve with a spoonful of mustard.
notes: Food safety: heat the ham until steaming hot throughout.

recipes.title: Finnish Lohikeitto Salmon Soup
recipes.summary: Creamy salmon and potato soup with dill and allspice.
steps: Soften the leek in the butter for 5 minutes, then add the carrot, potato, stock and allspice.
Simmer for 15 minutes, until the vegetables are tender.
Pour in the cream and add the salmon, then simmer gently for 4 minutes, until the salmon turns opaque.
Season, stir through the dill and serve.
notes: Food safety: cook the salmon until opaque throughout and keep it refrigerated until needed.

recipes.title: Swedish Hovmästarsås Mustard and Dill Sauce
recipes.summary: Sweet-sharp mustard and dill sauce for cured salmon, boiled potato and gravlax.
steps: Whisk the mustard, sugar, vinegar and a pinch of salt until the sugar has dissolved.
Slowly whisk in the oil in a thin stream until the sauce is thick and glossy.
Stir through the dill, season and chill for 30 minutes.
notes: Keep chilled in a jar for up to 5 days.

recipes.title: Finnish Rosolli Beetroot Salad
recipes.summary: Ruby diced beetroot, apple, potato and pickles in a creamy dressing.
steps: Boil the beetroots, potato and carrots for 25 minutes, until a knife slides in easily, then cool, peel and dice.
Whip the cream until soft peaks form, then stir in the vinegar, sugar, salt and pepper.
Toss the vegetables, apple, pickles and onion with the dressing and chill for 1 hour before serving.
notes: Serve cold, and keep refrigerated for up to 2 days.

recipes.title: Norwegian Eggerøre Soft Scrambled Eggs
recipes.summary: Very softly scrambled eggs on rye with chives and smoked salmon.
steps: Whisk the eggs, milk and seasoning in a bowl.
Melt the butter in a small pan over low heat and add the eggs, stirring slowly for 3 minutes until just set but still creamy.
Pile onto toasted rye, top with the smoked salmon and chives.
notes: Food safety: cook the eggs until just set with no liquid egg remaining, and keep the smoked salmon refrigerated until serving. Use fresh, uncracked eggs; for pregnant women, older people, young children and anyone with low immunity, cook the eggs until the yolks are firm.

recipes.title: Swedish Skagenröra Prawn and Dill Toast Topping
recipes.summary: Cold prawns folded through mayonnaise, dill and lemon over buttered toast.
steps: Mix the prawns, mayonnaise, sour cream, lemon juice, dill and onion until lightly bound.
Season with salt and white pepper, then chill for 15 minutes.
Toast the bread for 3 minutes until golden, butter it while hot and pile the prawn mixture on top.
notes: Food safety: use prawns that are cooked and kept refrigerated, and eat within 24 hours.

recipes.title: Danish Remoulade Sauce
recipes.summary: Curry-spiced pickle mayonnaise for fish fillets, roast pork and hot dogs.
steps: Stir the mayonnaise with the curry powder, mustard and lemon juice until smooth.
Fold through the pickles, capers and parsley.
Season, then chill for at least 20 minutes so the flavours settle.
notes: Keep chilled in a jar for up to 5 days.
